solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leader in Rome closer to Spanish Pope

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of Spanish is taken

parts.note: Adrian is the name of several popes, including the only English one, Adrian IV

explanation.surface: A papal title that seems to lean towards Spain, as if a Spanish pope were about to be chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer to Spanish' gives H, its last letter. The emperor in question was himself born in Spain, which gives the surface an extra edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman emperor, so he was a ruler who led the empire from Rome.

clue.text: Goddess in charge inspires book relating to Israelites

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the goddess takes the book inside her

parts.note: Hera was the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A goddess in authority motivates the writing of a book about the people of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the Hebrews, the ancient people of Israel, especially their language.

clue.text: Daughter on time to entertain adult film star

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within your home, so the adult sits inside

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A daughter turns up punctually to host a grown-up movie celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Donat was an English actor of the 1930s and 40s, an Oscar winner for Goodbye, Mr Chips.

clue.text: Hot dog makes you suffer

parts.note: something hot is fashionable, or in
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A hot dog snack that gives you an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot dog' reads as the snack, but it splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on yourself and undergo it.

clue.text: Nymphs in car heading north across main road

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching through its middle, so the road goes inside the car
in a down entry heading north means reading from bottom to top, so the car's letters run backwards

parts.note: a sedan is a saloon car
the A1 is Britain's longest main road, written with I for 1; in this down entry it too is read upwards with the car, giving IA

explanation.surface: Water spirits riding in a car travelling north over the A1.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns SEDAN into NADES, and 'across' puts the road inside; strictly the whole assembly SEDAIAN reads upwards, so A1 climbs too. The A1 runs from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are the water nymphs of Greek myth; this is the Greek-style plural of that word.

clue.text: Black cat runs for ball pitched short

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an ounce is the snow leopard
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dark cat dashing after a short-bouncing ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a delivery pitched short rears up at the batsman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a short-pitched delivery that rises sharply towards the batter is called by this name.

clue.text: Fabulous quartet without rhythm? Not entirely

parts.note: a beat is a musical rhythm

indicators.note: not entirely means not the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: less means without, as in 'a cup less its handle'

explanation.surface: Asking whether a famous foursome lacked rhythm, and answering not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' points to the band's nickname, the Fab Four.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liverpool band of John, Paul, George and Ringo were nicknamed the Fab Four.

clue.text: Continuous relaxation after new clubs opened by university

indicators.note: a sequence opened by something has that thing at its very start, so the university comes first
after means the relaxation follows the other pieces

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
an easing is a relaxation, as of tension or rules

explanation.surface: A university launches new clubs, followed by a period of unwinding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing never stops, which is to say it is continuous and without a break.

clue.text: Bird, huge one, climbing moment before storm

indicators.note: before means the moment comes ahead of the storm
in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird
mo is short for a moment, as in 'half a mo'
to storm is to rage or rant

explanation.surface: A great bird soaring up in the moment before a storm breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a dark, long-necked diving seabird.

clue.text: Help Resistance woman tempted to conceal priest

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide something within, so the priest goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
Eve was tempted by the serpent in Eden
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A member of the wartime Resistance, a woman, is drawn into hiding a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The priest goes between R and EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone in trouble is to aid them or ease their distress.

clue.text: Graduate adopting single feature creates fine porcelain

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the graduate's letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
single means one
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A graduate who takes up one design feature produces delicate china.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a translucent English porcelain made with ash from burnt animal bones.

clue.text: Marine animal takes fuel right inside

indicators.note: inside places the right-hand letter within the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: A sea creature absorbing fuel properly into itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is built by tiny sea creatures called polyps, and the word also names the creature itself.

clue.text: Changed later broadcast by news boss

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A news editor puts out a story later than planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something altered has been modified or made different, the past participle matching 'Changed'.

clue.text: Glance the French love

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
to adore is to love

explanation.surface: A quick look at the French, whom one loves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' looks like a quick look, but here it is a mineral name: galena is also called lead glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glance is a mining term for a lustrous ore; lead glance, or galena, is the main source of the metal.

clue.text: School dunces wanting these for geometry?

parts.note: a comp is a British comprehensive school
asses are fools or dunces

explanation.surface: Dim pupils at school lacking the right kit for a geometry lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: A comp is a British comprehensive, a state secondary school. 'wanting' just links the pieces to the definition, which leans on the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry students use a pair of hinged arms with a point and pencil to draw circles and arcs.

clue.text: Nice worker in motorway eatery?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written here with I for 1
a dinette is a small dining area

explanation.surface: A pleasant employee at a motorway service-station café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Parisian shop girl or seamstress, so a French working woman, as one might find in Nice.

clue.text: Cunning fellows housed in suitable accommodation

indicators.note: being housed in something means living inside it, so these pieces go within the suitable word

parts.note: apt means suitable
art can mean cunning or trickery, as in 'arts and wiles'
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Crafty men lodged in fitting rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, or a set of rooms to live in, is a form of living accommodation.

clue.text: Mad son to be released? That's pointless

indicators.note: a son who is released is let go from the word, so that letter is removed

parts.note: insane means mad

explanation.surface: A madman's son about to be freed from an asylum, which seems senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane remarks are silly and lacking in sense or purpose.

clue.text: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour

definitions.text: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour

parts.words: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour
parts.note: a many-headed serpent that grew new heads whenever one was cut off, killed as the second labour of Hercules; Labour is not the political party

explanation.surface: Something revived after spending cuts, only to be scrapped by the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests British politics and austerity, but the cuts are sword blows and the Labour is one of the twelve tasks of Hercules.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Lernaean monster regrew heads when they were severed until Hercules destroyed it.

clue.text: Starr reportedly had taste for this meat back in short supply

definitions.text: Starr reportedly had taste for this

parts.note: ham is a cured meat

indicators.note: short supply of a word means its final letter is missing, so the end is cut off

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A meat said to be the comedian's favourite, now running low.
explanation.walkthrough: Freddie Starr was a British comedian; the Sun newspaper's famous 1986 headline was 'Freddie Starr ate my hamster'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid story claimed the comedian had eaten a small pet rodent, so it was what he supposedly had a taste for.

clue.text: Warplane circling about cargo ship

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the warplane surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a fighter is a military aircraft
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A military jet circling overhead around a vessel carrying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a vessel built to carry goods rather than passengers.

clue.text: Scientist, absent-minded, departs for West

indicators.note: one thing put for another replaces it, so the departing letter takes the western letter's place

parts.note: a faraway look is absent-minded or dreamy
W is the compass abbreviation for west
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A dreamy scientist leaves for the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Faraday was the English physicist and chemist who discovered electromagnetic induction.

clue.text: Having slap-up meal but missing first course

indicators.note: missing first means the opening letter is absent

parts.note: feasting is eating a lavish meal

explanation.surface: Enjoying a lavish dinner but skipping the starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first course' reads as the starter, but 'first' belongs with 'missing' and 'course' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In navigation, an easting is distance run due east, a course made towards the east.

clue.text: Perverse desire to inter upper-class remains

indicators.note: to inter is to bury, so the letter is placed inside the rearranged word
perverse means twisted or contrary, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class, as in 'U and non-U'

explanation.surface: A twisted urge to bury the remains of a posh person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perverse' makes RESIDE from DESIRE, and 'to inter' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over after the rest has gone, so it means the leftovers.

clue.text: Enormous creature in gym on steroids

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the words that follow, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A huge brute at the gym, pumped up on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast of frightening size is a fair description of a giant, fearsome being.

clue.text: Pigs going outside had tails

indicators.note: the pigs go outside the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: sows are female pigs

explanation.surface: Pigs going out that had curly tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tails' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them closely and secretly, as a detective does.

clue.text: An Irishman seen in racial category

parts.note: an gives the article A
Ryan is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irish man noticed in an ethnic grouping.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was used in discredited racial theory for a supposed Indo-European ethnic group.

clue.text: Spiritual symbol I see in American city

parts.note: Om is the sacred syllable and symbol of Hinduism and Buddhism
aha is said when you realise something, like 'I see'

explanation.surface: Spotting a sacred emblem in a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska.

clue.text: One being taught French you support on course

parts.note: tu is the familiar French word for you
a tee supports a golf ball on the course

explanation.surface: A French student who supports you on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a pupil who is instructed by a tutor.

clue.text: Host returned to assist worker on farm

indicators.note: to means the assisting word is attached at the end
returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a host is a great number, a myriad
to aid is to assist

explanation.surface: A host comes back to help a farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a person entertaining guests but means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a woman employed to milk cows and make butter on a farm.

clue.text: Likes of Apollo warmly received in such a corridor

definitions.text: Likes of Apollo warmly received in such a corridor

parts.words: Likes of Apollo warmly received in such a corridor
parts.note: Apollo is the spacecraft, not the god; returning capsules heat up fiercely when coming back into the atmosphere through a narrow safe path

explanation.surface: The god Apollo and his kind welcomed warmly in a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmly received' is literal: the craft is heated by friction with the air on its way back.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft returning to Earth must hit a narrow band of approach angles, called the corridor, to survive descent.

clue.text: Rev with beer finds an edge at sea

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it hard
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A vicar with a pint finds himself on the brink at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a clergyman but is the engine verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of the side of a boat.
